thread:
deploy-bot: :rocket: Starting canary rollout v2.7.1 -> production. Canary group: r-infer-canary-12..r-infer-canary-20 (~5% traffic). Rolling in 10% increments.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Error rate spike detected for /v1/generate (canary group). 5xx rate 12% (baseline 0.3%). Source: nginx-prod-canary-14.
alice.chen: I'm on call. looking. tagging @devon_sre and @gina_ops.
devon_sre: grabbing logs from canary-14, running quick smoke. can everyone pause any manual traffic shifts?
ben.patel: noticed increased p50 latency as well from the new kernel. p50 went 60ms -> 420ms for short prompts.
carla_cs: support is getting customer reports: a handful of API keys returning 502s, one enterprise account reported timeouts on embed uploads. CX escalation is warm.
frank_runtime: pulling model server logs. seeing repeated kv-cache OOMs and then grpc retries. suspect quantized variant path regressing under load.
emma_pm: what's customer impact? percent of traffic and orgs affected?
alice.chen: current canary is ~5% of overall traffic. error budget crossing SLOs for canary tier. product tier customers impacted ~0.04% of requests but one enterprise flow hit timeouts.
gina_ops: recommend immediate backoff to prevent wider blast. Options: 1) flip feature flag to disable v2.7.1 for canary, 2) drain canary traffic to previous version, 3) force rollback artifact. thoughts?
devon_sre: prefer safe backout: toggle flag + drain. less blast radius than a full rollback. we can run incremental drain and watch errors.
alice.chen: agree. Action plan: (A) flip canary flag to off (B) drain canary with traffic-shift to v2.6.9 over 2 mins (C) run smoke tests (D) if stable, stop rollout and open follow-up. I'll coordinate.
frank_runtime: command to flip flag in the ops console:
```
# toggle rollout.canary.v2_7_1.enabled = false
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_API" https://ops.redwood.internal/flags/rollout.canary.v2_7_1/disable
```
frank_runtime: or via featureflag CLI: `ff toggle rollout.canary.v2_7_1 --off --actor alice.chen`
carla_cs: I'll let affected customers know we're rolling back the canary and will update once stable.
ben.patel: initiating drain: `rctl traffic-shift --from canary-group --to stable --duration 120s`
incident-bot: :information_source: Traffic shift started by ben.patel. Old: canary-12..20 -> stable pool. Expected finish in 2m.
devon_sre: watching metrics: error-rate on /v1/generate dropping... p50 coming down on canary traces. good sign.
emma_pm: is billing impacted? any need to notify account managers?
carla_cs: notifying AMs for the one enterprise org. CS message: "We observed transient timeouts during a canary rollout; we've drained canary and reverted traffic. No data loss. We will follow up."
alice.chen: smoke tests: running curl + small-cases against a sample of canary nodes now.
frank_runtime: logs show OOMs stopped after traffic drain. kv-cache pressure normalizing.
devon_sre: will run a verification checklist: 1) 5xx rate back to baseline on canary logs, 2) end-to-end request success for affected API keys, 3) confirm no new deploys to canary. Posting checklist results when done.
ben.patel: traffic-shift completed.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Traffic shift finished at 2534568045. Canary group now at 0% v2.7.1.
devon_sre: verification 1: canary 5xx rate 0.4% now (close to baseline). verification 2: ran E2E for 3 affected API keys; all responses 200 within expected latency. verification 3: release pipeline shows v2.7.1 halted for canary.
alice.chen: marking incident status: MITIGATED. keeping channel open for 1 hour for stability and then will hand off to postmortem.
carla_cs: customers messaged, no critical escalations. one partner still wants a brief call tomorrow.
emma_pm: please capture root-cause suspects: quantized variant selection under specific prompt-length distribution and cache pressure + a kernel path regression. schedule triage with runtime/infra.
frank_runtime: will capture logs and model variant configs and open an urgent bug in our tracker (S-12345). attaching sample logs.
gina_ops: adding follow-up tasks: revert candidate removed from canary pool, quarantine image in registry, block auto-rollout triggers until fix.
devon_sre: recommend we don't push v2.7.1 to dedicated/dedicated-beta until regression validated.
alice.chen: oncall shift: I'm handing to @gina_ops for long tail monitoring. I'll update the incident doc and create postmortem ticket. If anyone sees regression pop back, page the oncall.
gina_ops: taking handoff. I'll monitor for the next 60m and escalate if anything recurs.
carla_cs: thanks everyone, closing customer updates channel and will follow up with the partner.
alice.chen: final note: no rollback artifact required since we drained canary and traffic is on stable. Marking this as "canary backoff & drain" mitigation. moving to postmortem. (reacted :thumbsup:)
